home.html:
What is Guitariz Studio?

Guitariz Studio is a free, browser-based music toolkit built for guitarists, songwriters, producers, and music students who want professional-grade audio analysis without a subscription. Instead of paying for desktop software or juggling multiple subscription apps, you get automated chord recognition, neural stem separation, an interactive scale and raga explorer, and practice utilities in one unified hub—running entirely through your web browser.

The project started as an open-source initiative by Abhinav Vaidya to make advanced audio processing tools (chord detection engines, source separation models, harmonic visualizers) freely accessible to anyone learning or creating music. It remains 100% free and open-source with an active contributor community.

Who Uses Guitariz Studio

  • Songwriters & Transcribers: Extracting chord progressions, detected key signatures, and tempo from reference audio or YouTube streams.
  • Guitar & Bass Students: Visualizing scale patterns, chord voicings, and modal frameworks across interactive 2D and 3D fretboards.
  • Producers & Vocalists: Generating clean vocal acapellas or isolated instrumental backing stems without expensive software licenses.
  • Music Theorists: Exploring comparative theory bridges between Western diatonic modes and Hindustani Classical Ragas.

Core Studio Tools

Chord AI — Upload audio (MP3, WAV, FLAC) or paste YouTube links to extract chord progressions, powered by Librosa harmonic-percussive analysis and Viterbi HMM smoothing.

Stem Splitter — Separate audio into up to 6 distinct stems (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other) using Meta AI's Demucs deep learning model.

Scale Explorer — Map Western modes, pentatonics, and Indian Classical Thaats across an interactive guitar fretboard in real time.

Why It's Free

Guitariz Studio operates on an open-access philosophy. Core AI chord transcription, stem separation, and theory utilities remain completely free forever without paywalls or mandatory account signups.

chordAi.title: Chord AI Free - Online Chord Finder & Audio Recognition | Guitariz
chordAi.description: Free AI chord finder and song transcriber. Extract chords, tempo, and key signatures from MP3s and YouTube with our online chord recognition tool.
chordAi.tagline: Online AI chord finder & harmonic transcriber. Extract guitar chords and keys automatically from MP3s or YouTube.
chordAi.html:
How Chord AI Works

Most basic chord detectors rely on rudimentary pitch-class profiling, leading to frequent errors on complex musical arrangements. Guitariz Chord AI employs a robust digital signal processing pipeline built on Librosa: Harmonic-Percussive Source Separation (HPSS) isolates harmonic tonal content from transient drum noise, Constant-Q chroma features are extracted from the harmonic stream, and pitch distributions are matched against harmonic chord templates.

Viterbi HMM Smoothing: Raw frame-by-frame chord estimates are regularized using a log-space Viterbi-based Hidden Markov Model. This ensures musically plausible transitions and eliminates erratic fractional-second chord fluttering.

From Audio Files or YouTube: Upload local MP3, WAV, or FLAC audio files or paste a YouTube URL—the engine decodes, analyzes, and synchronizes the chord progression timeline automatically.

Neural Network Roadmap: A CRNN (Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network) architecture is in development to provide an additional neural recognition mode alongside the current DSP baseline, deployable via ONNX Runtime.

Chord AI vs. the Chord Finder

Chord AI listens to a recording and writes out the chords. If you already have notes under your fingers, such as a fret shape you are unsure about, use the Chord Finder instead: pick the notes on a guitar neck or piano and it names the chord, including inversions.

What You Get

  • Full synchronized chord timeline synced to audio playback
  • Detected primary key signature and mode
  • Estimated tempo (BPM)
  • Standard chord notation symbols (Major, Minor, 7, maj7, m7, sus4, dim, aug)

How Stem Separation Works

Stem separation decomposes a finished stereo mix into its individual multi-track components. Guitariz Stem Separator utilizes Meta AI's open-source Demucs architecture—a hybrid time-domain and frequency-domain deep neural network trained on isolated multi-tracks to distinguish overlapping acoustic sources in dense mixes.

6-Stem Source Extraction

Unlike standard 2-stem tools, our full separation mode isolates up to 6 distinct stems:

  • Vocals: Clean lead vocals and harmonies isolated from instrumental backing.
  • Drums: Full percussive track including kick, snare, toms, and cymbals.
  • Bass: Isolated bass guitar and sub-bass synthesizers for bass transcribers.
  • Guitar: Electric and acoustic guitar layers separated from keys and synths.
  • Piano: Acoustic piano and electric keyboard tracks.
  • Other: Remaining synths, brass, strings, and ambient effects.

Privacy & Temporary Storage

Uploaded audio files are processed statelessly and temporary stem download bundles are purged automatically after processing finishes.

Fast AI Vocal Isolation & Instrumental Extraction

Guitariz Vocal Splitter extracts crystal-clear lead vocals and high-fidelity instrumental backing tracks from any song using neural source separation. Designed for vocalists, producers, and karaoke creators, the model cleanly divides mixed audio without hollow phasing or muffled high frequencies.

The Demucs Separation Architecture

The processing pipeline uses Meta AI's Demucs neural network. Demucs operates on raw audio waveforms using multi-scale convolutional encoders and bidirectional LSTM recurrent layers to model long-range harmonic dependencies, separating dense vocal layers that traditional EQ phase-cancellation tools fail to isolate.

Key Applications

  • Karaoke Backing Tracks: Strip lead vocals completely while maintaining the full dynamic impact of the rhythm section and guitars.
  • Acapella Extraction: Isolate pristine vocal stems for sampling, remixing, and vocal production.
  • Instrument Practice: Mute vocals to rehearse singing lead or practicing along with reference tracks.

bpmDetector.title: Free Online BPM Detector & Tap Tempo Finder | Guitariz
bpmDetector.description: Detect the exact BPM (tempo) of any MP3 or audio file online for free. Features real-time DSP audio beat detection and tap tempo sync.
bpmDetector.tagline: Instant client-side DSP tempo analysis and tap tempo calculation.
bpmDetector.html:
Instant In-Browser BPM Detection

Guitariz Online BPM Detector measures the exact tempo (beats per minute) of any song or audio file directly in your browser. Audio analysis runs locally through the Web Audio API without server upload queues, delivering private and immediate tempo detection.

The Multi-Band DSP Detection Pipeline

The client-side tempo estimation engine uses a specialized multi-stage audio processing pipeline:

  • Dual-Band IIR Butterworth Filtering: The audio signal is filtered using 2nd-order Direct Form II IIR filters into a sub-bass band (220 Hz low-pass for kick drums and 808s) and a mid-percussion band (1200 Hz band-pass for snares and acoustic slaps).
  • Weber-Fechner Logarithmic Energy Compression: Short-term RMS energy envelopes are compressed logarithmically to emulate human psychoacoustic loudness perception.
  • Autocorrelation & Multi-Harmonic Resonant Comb Filter: The combined onset strength signal is autocorrelated across lag frames and evaluated through a multi-harmonic resonant comb filter across the 52–210 BPM range.
  • Dynamic Beat Alignment: Candidate tempos are scored against dynamic downbeat phase grids to verify metric consistency.

Interactive Tap Tempo

Tap along manually to any rhythm or live acoustic performance. The tap engine tracks consecutive tap intervals and calculates a rolling running average for accurate real-time tempo measurement.

keyDetector.description: Find the key of any song or audio file for free. AI-powered musical key recognition and scale mode detector for musicians and producers.
keyDetector.tagline: Harmonic chromagram profiling and tonal key center detection.
keyDetector.html:
Accurate Musical Key & Tonality Detection

Identifying the musical key and tonal center of an audio track is critical for vocal tuning, harmonic mixing, remixing, and instrument solos. Guitariz Online Key Detector analyzes audio chromagrams to find the primary key signature and modal tonality.

How Key Detection Operates

  • Pitch-Class Chromagram Extraction: The audio spectrum is mapped into 12 discrete pitch classes across multiple octaves, measuring the cumulative energy of each musical pitch.
  • Harmonic Key-Profile Correlation: The aggregated pitch profile is mathematically correlated against standardized major and minor tonal hierarchy profiles across all 24 musical keys.
  • Tonic & Relative Key Resolution: The engine compares tonic weightings against relative major/minor pairs to resolve ambiguous key centers and modal shifts accurately.

theory.title: Interactive Circle of Fifths - Guided Music Theory Lab | Guitariz
theory.description: Master functional harmony with our interactive Circle of Fifths lab. Explore key signatures, modulations, chord families, and diatonic relationships.
theory.tagline: Interactive Circle of Fifths and functional harmony learning lab.
theory.html:
Mastering Functional Harmony with the Circle of Fifths

The Circle of Fifths organizes the 12 chromatic pitches into an intuitive geometric circle of ascending perfect fifths (clockwise) and descending perfect fourths (counter-clockwise). Guitariz Theory Lab provides an interactive, audio-enabled environment for songwriters, guitarists, and music students to master functional harmony.

Core Music Theory Concepts

  • Key Signatures & Accidentals: Moving clockwise from C Major adds sharps (G=1♯, D=2♯, A=3♯), while moving counter-clockwise adds flats (F=1♭, B♭=2♭, E♭=3♭).
  • Diatonic Chord Families: For any selected root, the circle highlights primary triads—Tonic (I), Subdominant (IV), and Dominant (V)—alongside secondary minor chords (ii, iii, vi).
  • Pivot Chord Modulation: Neighboring keys share six common diatonic notes, making adjacent circle positions ideal for harmonic transitions.
  • Relative Minor Keys: The inner ring displays relative minor keys sharing the identical key signature with their major relative.

ragaTheory.title: Indian Ragas & Western Scales: The Music Theory Bridge | Guitariz
ragaTheory.description: Hindustani Thaat System & Western Modes: A Comparative Guide. Compare Bilawal, Yaman, Kafi, Bhairav, and other Indian Ragas to Western music modes.
ragaTheory.tagline: Comparative guide bridging Hindustani Classical Thaats with Western diatonic modes.
ragaTheory.html:
Bridging Hindustani Classical Thaats and Western Diatonic Modes

Indian Classical music (Hindustani) and Western music theory share identical twelve-semitone chromatic divisions despite differing terminology and aesthetic traditions. Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande formalized the 10 parent heptatonic scales (Thaats), which form the foundational classification for North Indian Ragas.

The 10 Thaats & Their Western Modal Equivalents

  • Bilawal Thaat: Equivalent to the Western Ionian Mode (Major Scale) [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].
  • Kalyan Thaat: Equivalent to the Lydian Mode with sharp fourth (Teevra Ma) [1, 2, 3, ♯4, 5, 6, 7].
  • Khamaj Thaat: Equivalent to the Mixolydian Mode with flat seventh (Komal Ni) [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ♭7].
  • Kafi Thaat: Equivalent to the Dorian Mode with flat third and flat seventh [1, 2, ♭3, 4, 5, 6, ♭7].
  • Asavari Thaat: Equivalent to the Aeolian Mode (Natural Minor Scale) [1, 2, ♭3, 4, 5, ♭6, ♭7].
  • Bhairavi Thaat: Equivalent to the Phrygian Mode [1, ♭2, ♭3, 4, 5, ♭6, ♭7].
  • Altered Thaats (Bhairav, Poorvi, Todi, Marwa): Feature double-harmonic and augmented fourth intervals characteristic of Indian Classical ragas.

Real-Time Chromatic Instrument Tuner

Autocorrelation Pitch Detection Engine

Incoming microphone audio streams are analyzed using time-domain autocorrelation with parabolic peak interpolation:

  • Cents-Level Accuracy: Calculates pitch deviation within 1 cent relative to standard $A_4 = 440\text{ Hz}$ concert pitch (adjustable from 430 Hz to 450 Hz).
  • Target String Guides: Includes visual tuning guides for standard 6-string guitar ($E_2, A_2, D_3, G_3, B_3, E_4$), bass, and custom alternate tunings.

chordFinder.title: Chord Finder – Identify Chords from Notes (Guitar & Piano)
chordFinder.description: Pick notes on a guitar fretboard or piano and instantly see the chord name, alternate names and voicings. Free, no signup. Or detect chords from audio.
chordFinder.intro: Pick notes on a guitar neck or piano keyboard and get the chord name instantly, including inversions and slash chords. Free, no signup.
chordFinder.html:
How to Find a Chord from Notes

Every chord is a stack of intervals above a root note. A major chord is a root, a major third (four semitones up) and a perfect fifth (seven semitones up). Swap the major third for a minor third (three semitones) and you get a minor chord. To identify an unknown chord, find the root, measure the other notes against it and match the pattern. The chord finder does this for you as you click.

The lowest note you pick is treated as the bass. If the bass is not the root, the result is shown as a slash chord: C/E is a C major chord with E in the bass, also called first inversion.

Using the Chord Finder on Guitar

Select a fret (or the open string) on each string you play. Strings you leave unselected are treated as muted. Voicings that leave out the fifth, which is common for seventh chords, are still recognized, so C–E–B on three strings is correctly read as Cmaj7.

Using the Chord Finder on Piano

Switch to the piano keyboard and click the keys you want. The chord finder reads the pitch classes you select, ignores octave doubling and names the chord the same way it does for guitar.

Common Chord Types

  • Major: root, major 3rd, perfect 5th (C–E–G)
  • Minor: root, minor 3rd, perfect 5th (C–E♭–G)
  • Dominant 7th: major triad plus a minor 7th (C–E–G–B♭)
  • Major 7th: major triad plus a major 7th (C–E–G–B)
  • Minor 7th: minor triad plus a minor 7th (C–E♭–G–B♭)
  • Sus2 and Sus4: the third is replaced by a 2nd or a 4th (C–D–G, C–F–G)
  • Diminished: root, minor 3rd, diminished 5th (C–E♭–G♭)
  • Augmented: root, major 3rd, augmented 5th (C–E–G♯)
  • Power chord (5): root and perfect 5th only (C–G)

Why One Set of Notes Can Have Several Names

A–C–E–G is Am7, while C–E–G–A is C6. These are the same four pitch classes, and the right name depends on the bass note and the musical context. The chord finder uses your lowest note to choose the most likely name and lists the other common names underneath.

Have a Song Instead of Notes?

If you want the chords of a recording rather than a shape you are holding, use Chord AI, which detects chords from an MP3 or YouTube link. To work out which key a song is in, try the key detector, explore notes on the neck with the interactive fretboard, or build progressions with the chord progression generator.

faqs.q: How does the chord finder work?
faqs.a: It takes the notes you select, removes duplicates across octaves, and compares the pattern of intervals against known chord formulas such as major, minor, seventh, sus and diminished. The most common matching name is shown first.

faqs.q: Does it recognize inversions and slash chords?
faqs.a: Yes. The lowest note you select is treated as the bass. If it is not the root, the chord is shown as a slash chord. For example, E–G–C is shown as C/E, a first inversion of C major.

faqs.q: Why does it sometimes show more than one name?
faqs.a: Some sets of notes can be named in more than one valid way. A–C–E–G can be read as Am7 or as C6 with A in the bass. The finder picks the most likely name from your bass note and lists the other common names.

faqs.q: Do I need to select all six strings?
faqs.a: No. Select only the strings you play and leave the rest muted. Three- and four-note voicings work, and common chords that leave out the fifth, such as Cmaj7 or C7, are still recognized.

faqs.q: Does the chord finder work for piano?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to the piano keyboard and click the keys. Piano and guitar use the same detection, so the same notes give the same chord name.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the chord finder and Chord AI?
faqs.a: The chord finder names a chord from notes you pick. Chord AI listens to an audio file or YouTube link and detects the chords played in the recording.

faqs.q: Why does it say no standard chord matches?
faqs.a: The notes you picked do not fit a standard chord name, for example a tight cluster of neighbouring notes. Try removing or changing one note. When one note is the likely culprit, the finder suggests the closest chords.
